Surah At-Tawbah (Repentance) [Madaniyyah (revealed in Medina) except the last two verses, which are Makkiyyah; it has 129 verses; it was revealed after al-Ma'idah]. The basmalah (the formula "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate") is not written at its beginning, because the Prophet (ﷺ) did not command it to be written, as is derived from a hadith narrated by al-Hakim, who also transmitted a report with similar meaning from Ali that the basmalah is a declaration of security (amān), and it was revealed to lift security by the sword. And from Hudhayfah: "You call it Surat at-Tawbah, but it is Surat al-Adhab (the Surah of Punishment)." Al-Bukhari narrated from al-Bara' that it was the last surah to be revealed.

This is a declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger ﴿directed to those with whom you made covenants among the polytheists﴾, whether the covenant was unrestricted, or for less than four months, or for more than that. The wording of the covenant is as mentioned in His saying:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 2:

﴿So travel﴾ (fasihu), i.e., go about safely, O polytheists, ﴿in the land for four months﴾, the first of which is Shawwal, as indicated by what follows, and there is no safe conduct (aman) for you after them. ﴿And know that you cannot escape Allah﴾, i.e., you cannot escape His punishment, ﴿and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾, humiliating them in this world by killing and in the other by the Fire.

Proclamation (ʾadhān, i.e., announcement) from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the Day of the Greatest Pilgrimage, the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists (al-mushrikīn) and their treaties, and likewise His Messenger. "The Prophet ﷺ had sent ʿAlī in the year nine (sanat tisʿ) and he proclaimed on the Day of Sacrifice at Minā these verses, and that no polytheist should perform Hajj after this year, and that no one should circumambulate the House naked." Narrated by al-Bukhari. ﴿So if you repent﴾ from disbelief ﴿it is better for you; but if you turn away﴾ from faith ﴿then know that you will not cause Allah to fail﴾ ﴿and give tidings﴾ inform ﴿to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾ painful, which is killing and captivity in this world, and the Fire in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 4:

﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists, then they have not failed you in anything of the terms of the covenant, nor have they supported anyone against you⁠—﴾ from the conditions of the covenant. ﴿Then fulfil to them their covenant until⁠﴾ the expiry of ﴿their term⁠﴾ which you agreed upon. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the God-fearing﴾ by fulfilling covenants.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, "the exegesis of the two Jalals") on Surah 9, verse 5:**

﴿Then when the sacred months have passed﴾ (فَإذا انْسَلَخَ) meaning went out (خَرَجَ), ﴿the sacred months﴾ (الأَشْهُر الحُرُم), and they are the last period of the respite (آخِر مُدَّة التَّأْجِيل). ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ (فاقْتُلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وجَدْتُمُوهُمْ), whether in a permitted area or in the sacred precinct (haram) (فِي حِلّ أوْ حَرَم). ﴿And seize them﴾ (وخُذُوهُمْ) by taking them captive (بِالأَسْرِ). ﴿And besiege them﴾ (واحْصُرُوهُمْ) in fortresses and strongholds (فِي القِلاع والحُصُون), until they are compelled to choose between death and Islam (حَتّى يُضْطَرُّوا إلى القَتْل أوْ الإسْلام). ﴿And lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾ (واقْعُدُوا لَهُمْ كُلّ مَرْصَد), meaning a route they take (طَرِيق يَسْلُكُونَهُ). The word كُلّ here is in the accusative (نُصِبَ) by removal of the governing preposition (نَزْع الخافِض, the dropping of a preposition so that the noun takes the accusative). ﴿But if they repent﴾ (فَإنْ تابُوا) from disbelief (مِن الكُفْر), ﴿and establish prayer and give zakat﴾ (وأَقامُوا الصَّلاة وآتَوْا الزَّكاة), ﴿then let them go their way﴾ (فَخَلُّوا سَبِيلهمْ), and do not harass them (ولا تَتَعَرَّضُوا لَهُمْ). ﴿Indeed, Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾ (إنّ اللَّه غَفُور رَحِيم) to whoever repents (لِمَن تابَ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 6:

﴿And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection﴾ (wa-in aḥad min al-mushrikīn) is in the nominative case (marfūʿ), governed by a verb implied by the verb that follows it, which explains it: ﴿seeks your protection﴾ (istajārak), i.e., asks you for safe conduct (istaʾmanak) from being killed. ﴿Then grant him protection﴾ (fa-ajirhu), i.e., give him security (aminhu) ﴿until he hears the words of Allah﴾ (kalām Allāh), the Qur'an, ﴿then convey him to his place of safety﴾ (thumma ablighhu maʾmanah), which is the abode of his people, if he does not believe, so that he may consider his affair. ﴿That﴾ (dhālika), the aforementioned (al-madhkūr), is ﴿because they are a people who do not know﴾ (bi-annahum qawm lā yaʿlamūn), the religion of Allah. So they must hear the Qur'an in order that they may know.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 7:

﴿How⦆ i.e., no: ﴿there can be for the polytheists a covenant with Allah and with His Messenger﴾ while they are disbelievers in Allah and His Messenger and treacherous, ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, and they are the Quraysh, who were excepted earlier, ﴿so long as they remain true to you﴾ i.e., they abide by the covenant and do not break it. Here "ma" is a conditional particle (shartiyyah), ﴿so be true to them. Surely Allah loves the godfearing﴾ in fulfilling it. The Prophet (ﷺ) remained true to their covenant until they broke it by aiding the Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah.

How can they have a covenant (with you), when, if they gain the upper hand over you, they will not observe regarding you any tie of kinship or any pact? (The clause "if they gain the upper hand over you," i.e. prevail over you, is a circumstantial clause, ḥāl.) They will not observe (yurāqibū, "observe" or "respect") regarding you any tie of kinship (qarābah) or any pact (dhimmah, i.e. covenant), but rather they will harm you as much as they are able. They please you with their mouths, with their fine words, while their hearts refuse (ta'ba, "refuse") to fulfil it, and most of them are defiant breakers of the covenant (fāsiqūn, i.e. nāqiḍūn lil-ʿahd).

﴿They have exchanged the signs of God﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿for a small price﴾ of this world, meaning they abandoned following it in favour of their appetites and desires, ﴿and they have averted [others] from His way﴾, His religion. ﴿Indeed, evil is﴾ what ﴿they have been doing﴾, ﴿their deed this﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 11:

﴿Then if they repent, establish the prayer, and give the zakat, they are your brothers in religion.﴾ That is, they are your brothers in the religion. ﴿And We detail the verses for a people who know.﴾ That is, we make clear the verses for a people who reflect.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 12:

﴿And if they break their oaths﴾ (nakathū) ﴿after their pledge﴾, i.e., they break (naqaḍū) ﴿their oaths﴾, meaning their covenants, ﴿and attack your religion﴾ (ṭa'anū fī dīnikum), i.e., they find fault with it, ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾ (a'immat al-kufr), i.e., their chiefs in it. The apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun here. ﴿Indeed, they have no oaths﴾, i.e., covenants, ﴿for them﴾. In another reading, it is recited with a kasra (innahum lā aymāna lahum, with the hamza of ayman read in the kasra form). ﴿So that they may desist﴾ (la'allahum yantahūna) ﴿from disbelief﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 13:

﴿Will you not fight﴾ (ألا) here is for urging (lit-tahdid, exhortation), ﴿a people who broke﴾ their oaths (nakathu), i.e., violated ﴿their oaths﴾, meaning their covenants, ﴿and they resolved to expel the Messenger﴾ from Makkah, when they consulted about it in the Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of the Quraysh), ﴿and they initiated [hostilities] against you﴾ with fighting ﴿first﴾, when they fought Khuza'ah, your allies, together with Banu Bakr. So what prevents you from fighting them? ﴿Do you fear them?﴾ (Atakhshawnahum), do you be afraid of them? ﴿Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ in abandoning fighting them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 14:

﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands⁠﴾ — He will kill them ﴿by your hands, and will disgrace them﴾ — He will humble them by capture and subjugation ﴿and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾ — by what He does to them; they are the Banu Khuza'ah.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 9, verse 15:

﴿And He will remove the rage of their hearts﴾ its distress (كربها), ﴿and Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills﴾ by their returning to Islam, like Abu Sufyan.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 16:

﴿Am﴾ (or) is here in the sense of the interrogative hamza of denial, ﴿Did you suppose that you would be left alone﴾, ﴿while Allah had not yet known﴾ (i.e., had not yet made known, in the sense of manifest knowledge), ﴿those of you who strove﴾ sincerely, ﴿and took no intimate friend other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers﴾ (waliyyah: confidants and allies). The meaning is: the sincere ones will not be made manifest, and they are those described by what has been mentioned, distinct from others.

It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God, [the word "mosques" being read in both the singular and the plural, referring to entering and sitting in them], bearing witness against themselves with disbelief. Those, their deeds have failed (بطلت, batalat, "became void"), because the condition for their validity is absent.
﴿Indeed, those who maintain the mosques of God are only those who believe in God and the Last Day, establish the prayer, give the zakat, and fear no one.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 19:

﴿Do you consider the giving of water to the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque﴾ to be ﴿like one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah?﴾ That is, the people of that (i.e., those who do such things) ﴿are not equal in the sight of Allah﴾ in merit. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, the disbelievers. It was revealed in rebuttal of the one who said that, and he was al-'Abbas or someone else.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 9, verse 20:

﴿Those who believe, emigrate, and strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their selves are greater in* **daraja** (degree) ﴾ rank (rutba) ﴿with God﴾ than others ﴿and those are the triumphant﴾, those who attain good.

*The Arabic word *daraja* is glossed here as rank (*rutba*).
﴿Their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him, and of approval, and of gardens for them, wherein is enduring bliss﴾ lasting.
{Khālidīna} (abiding eternally) is a qualifying state (ḥāl) that is anticipated (muqaddara), since they were not yet abiding at the moment of the promise.

It was revealed concerning those who abandoned the emigration (hijra) for the sake of their families and their trade: ﴿O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer﴾ disbelief, i.e., they chose it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 24:

﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, and your kinsfolk,﴾ your relatives. And in another reading, "your clans" (ʿashīrātukum). ﴿and the wealth you have acquired,﴾ that you have earned; ﴿and the commerce you fear will slump,﴾ that it will not be sold; ﴿and the dwellings you are pleased with, are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause,﴾ so that you remain behind for their sake from emigration (hijrah) and holy struggle (jihad); ﴿then wait﴾ await; ﴿until Allah brings His command.﴾ This is a threat to them.

﴿Indeed, Allah had given you victory on many battlefields﴾ for the war, ﴿such as Badr, Quraizah and al-Nadir﴾. ﴿And [remember] the day of Hunayn﴾, a valley between Makkah and al-Ta'if, meaning the day you fought the Hawazin there, and that was in Shawwal of the eighth year [after the Hijrah]. ﴿When﴾ is a *badal* (substitution, a grammatical term for a word that replaces and restates a preceding one) for "the day". ﴿Your large number impressed you﴾, so you said, "We will not be defeated today because of few numbers." They were twelve thousand, while the disbelievers were four thousand. ﴿But it availed you nothing, and the earth constricted for you despite its vastness﴾. The *ma* (مَا) here is a *masdariyyah* (verbal-noun particle, which turns the following clause into a verbal noun), meaning "with its expanse", that is, with its breadth and spaciousness. So you found no place in which you could be at ease, because of the severity of the fear that overtook you. ﴿Then you turned back in retreat﴾, defeated. The Prophet (ﷺ) remained on his white mule, with no one with him except al-Abbas and Abu Sufyan, who was holding its bridle.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 26:

﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility⁠﴾ (ṭumaʾnīnatahu, His serenity) ﴿upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾, so they returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) when al-ʿAbbās called out to them, by His permission, and they fought. ﴿And He sent down hosts you did not see﴾ (malāʾika, angels), ﴿and He punished those who disbelieved﴾ by killing and capture.
﴿Then Allah will turn in forgiveness after that to whomever He wills﴾ from among them, by Islam.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 28:

﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean﴾ — filth (qadhar), because of the corruption of their inner selves — ﴿so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque﴾, i.e., let them not enter the Haram ﴿after this, their year﴾, the year nine after the Hijrah ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, i.e., destitution, through the cutting off of their trade from you ﴿then Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills﴾, and He had enriched them through the conquests and the jizyah (poll tax on non-Muslim subjects).

﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day﴾, and if they did, they would have believed in the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿Nor do they forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden﴾, such as wine. ﴿Nor do they follow the religion of truth﴾, the established religion that abrogates (*naskh*) the other religions, which is the religion of Islam. ﴿From﴾ is a *bayān* (explanatory clarification) of ﴿those﴾. ﴿Those who were given the Scripture﴾, i.e., the Jews and the Christians. ﴿Until they pay the jizya﴾ (poll tax), the *kharāj* (tax) imposed upon them every year. ﴿With their own hands﴾ is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial phrase), meaning submissively, or "with their own hands," not entrusting it to others. ﴿While they are humbled﴾, abased and subject to the rule of Islam.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 30:

﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah."﴾ Jesus ﴿That is their statement from their mouths﴾, having no evidence for it. Rather, ﴿they imitate﴾, they resemble with it ﴿the saying of those who disbelieved before﴾, from their forefathers, following them blindly. ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾, may He curse them. ﴿How are they deluded?﴾, how are they turned away from the truth despite the presence of the proof?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 31:

﴿They took their rabbis﴾ (scholars of the Jews) ﴿and their monks﴾ (worshippers of the Christians) ﴿as lords besides Allah﴾, in that they followed them in making lawful what Allah had made unlawful and in making unlawful what He had made lawful. ﴿And [they took] the Messiah, son of Mary﴾, ﴿while they were not commanded except to worship﴾ in the Torah and the Gospel ﴿one God; there is no deity except Him, exalted is He﴾, glorified above [what they associate with Him].

﴿They want to extinguish the light of God﴾ [i.e., His sharia and His proofs] ﴿with their mouths﴾ [i.e., with their statements against it], ﴿but God refuses except to perfect His light﴾ [i.e., to make it manifest], ﴿even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ [that].

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 9, verse 33:

﴿He it is who sent His Messenger﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail﴾ (i.e., exalt it) ﴿over all religion﴾ all the religions that oppose it ﴿even though the polytheists dislike it﴾ that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 34:

﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the scholars (al-ahbar) and the monks (al-ruhban) consume the wealth of people unjustly﴾ they take it, ﴿and avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾ His religion. ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them﴾ i.e., the hoards, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ i.e., they do not pay their due from them, [namely] the zakah. ﴿So give them tidings﴾ inform them ﴿of a painful punishment﴾ painful, causing pain.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 35:

﴿On the Day when it will be heated up in the Fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it﴾ [i.e., burned with it], and their skins will be widened so that all of them are placed upon it. And it will be said to them: ﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard﴾, i.e., its recompense.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 36:

﴿Indeed, the number of months﴾ that are counted for the year ﴿with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah﴾ meaning the Preserved Tablet ﴿since the day He created the heavens and the earth. Of them﴾ i.e., of the months ﴿four are sacred﴾ forbidden: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram, and Rajab. ﴿That﴾ i.e., their sanctity ﴿is the upright religion﴾ the straight one. ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ i.e., in the sacred months, ﴿by committing sins,﴾ for sin in them is greater in burden; it was also said that it refers to all the months. ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together﴾ collectively, in every month ﴿as they fight against you all together. And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾ with help and victory.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 37:

﴿Indeed, the postponing (al-nasi') means the delaying of the sanctity of one month to another,﴾ as the Jahiliyya (the Age of Ignorance) used to do, delaying the sanctity of Muharram when it came in while they were fighting, until Safar. ﴿An increase in disbelief﴾ because of their disbelief in God's ruling concerning it. ﴿By it those who disbelieve are led astray﴾ (the verb being read with a ḍamma on the yā' and with a fatḥa), ﴿they make it lawful one year and make it unlawful another year﴾ — that is, the postponing — ﴿in order to match﴾ (yuwāṭi'ū, meaning they conform) ﴿the number of what God has made unlawful﴾ (the number of months), by making one month lawful and another unlawful in its place, so that they do not exceed four sacred months nor fall short of them, and they do not consider their specific identities. ﴿So they make lawful what God has made unlawful. Made attractive to them is the evil of their deeds﴾, so they considered it good.

It was revealed when the Prophet (ﷺ) called the people to the expedition of Tabuk, and they were in hardship and intense heat, so it was difficult for them: ﴿O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth?﴾ — with the assimilation of the tā' in the original (ithqaltum, from tathaqqaltum) into the thā' (ṯ) and the bringing in of the hamzat al-waṣl (the connecting hamza), meaning: you were slow and inclined away from jihad, ﴿to the earth﴾ and sitting in it. ﴿Are you satisfied with the life of this world﴾ and its pleasures? The interrogative is for reproach. ﴿Instead of the Hereafter﴾, i.e., in exchange for its bounties. ﴿Then the enjoyment of the life of this world, in comparison with the Hereafter, is but little﴾, insignificant.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 9, verse 39:

﴿Illa﴾ with the idgham (assimilation) of the lam of la (lā) into the nun of in (in, the conditional particle) in both places. ﴿Tanfiru﴾ means you go forth with the Prophet ﷺ for jihad. ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ meaning, a painful one. ﴿And will replace you with another people﴾ meaning, He will bring others in your place. ﴿And you will not harm Him﴾ meaning, Allah or the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿at all﴾ by abandoning his support, for Allah is the supporter of His religion. ﴿And Allah is competent over all things﴾ and among that is His support of His religion and His Prophet.

If you do not help him (the Prophet ﷺ), then Allah has already helped him when those who disbelieved expelled him from Makkah, forcing him to leave when they intended to kill him, imprison him, or banish him at the Assembly House (Dar al-Nadwa). He was the second of two (a state): one of them, and the other was Abu Bakr. The meaning: Allah helped him in that situation, so He will not forsake him in other situations. (When) "idh" is a substitute for the "idh" before it. They were both in the cave, a hollow in the mountain of Thawr. (When) "idh" is a second substitute: he said to his companion, Abu Bakr, who had said to him when he saw the feet of the polytheists: "If one of them were to look beneath his feet, he would see us": ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ through His help. Then Allah sent down His tranquility (sakinatahu), His reassurance, upon him. It is said this refers to the Prophet ﷺ, and it is said it refers to Abu Bakr. And He strengthened him, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, with hosts you did not see: angels in the cave and at the places of his fighting. And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest (al-sufla), the defeated, and the word of Allah, meaning the word of the testimony of faith, is the highest (al-'ulya), the manifest and victorious. And Allah is Mighty (aziz) in His dominion, Wise (hakim) in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 41:

﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ (in readiness and in unreadiness). It was said: (strong and weak), or (rich and poor). It is abrogated (mansukhah) by the verse ﴿There is no blame upon the weak﴾. ﴿And strive with your wealth and your lives in the way of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew﴾ that it is better for you; so do not be sluggish.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 42:

﴿Had it been﴾ something you invited them to, and it was revealed concerning the hypocrites who stayed behind, ﴿a gain﴾ a worldly good ﴿near﴾ easy to obtain ﴿and a journey of moderate length﴾ middling, ﴿they would have followed you﴾ seeking booty. ﴿But the distance seemed long to them﴾ the distance was far for them, so they stayed behind. ﴿And they will swear by God﴾ when you return to them, ﴿"Had we been able,"﴾ to go out, ﴿"we would have gone out with you." They destroy themselves﴾ by false swearing ﴿and God knows that they are indeed liars﴾ in their saying this.

The Prophet (ﷺ) had given permission to a group to stay behind, by his own ijtihad (independent judgement). So the verse came down as a rebuke to him, and it opened with pardon to reassure his heart: ﴿May Allah pardon you. Why did you give them permission?﴾ to stay behind; why did you not leave them alone? ﴿Until it becomes clear to you who are truthful﴾ in their excuse, ﴿and you know the liars﴾ in it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 9, verse 44:**

﴿Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission﴾ to be excused from ﴿striving with their wealth and their lives﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 45:

﴿Only those seek your permission (to stay behind) who do not believe in God and the Last Day, and whose hearts are in doubt⁠—﴾ doubted (shakkat) ﴿their hearts⁠﴾ concerning the religion, ﴿so in their doubt they waver⁠﴾ they are bewildered (yatahayyarun).

*Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 46:*

﴿And had they intended to go out﴾ with you, ﴿they would have prepared for it some preparation﴾ readiness (*uhbah*) of equipment and provisions. ﴿But Allah disliked their being sent forth﴾, meaning He did not will their going out, ﴿so He held them back﴾, meaning He made them sluggish. ﴿And it was said﴾, meaning it was said to them, ﴿"Sit with those who sit"﴾, meaning the sick, the women and the children. That is, Allah decreed that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 47:

﴿Had they gone out among you, they would have added to you nothing but corruption﴾, i.e., they would have corrupted you by discouraging the believers. ﴿And they would have hastened through the midst of you﴾, i.e., they would have hurried among you on foot, carrying tale-bearing (namimah). ﴿Seeking [to cause] you discord﴾, i.e., seeking for you ﴿fitnah﴾ by casting enmity [among you]. ﴿And among you are listeners to them﴾, i.e., those who accept what they say, listening with acceptance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 48:

﴿Indeed, they sought discord﴾ for you ﴿before [this]﴾, i.e., when you first came to Medina, ﴿and they turned over matters for you﴾, i.e., they devised plans against you and sought to nullify your religion, ﴿until the truth came﴾, i.e., the victory, ﴿and the command of Allah prevailed﴾, i.e., His religion became mighty, ﴿while they were averse﴾ to it, so they entered it outwardly.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 49:

﴿And among them is one who says, "Give me leave and do not put me to trial."﴾ That is, to stay behind (from the expedition). He is al-Jadd ibn Qays. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Would you like to fight the yellow-skinned people (Banu al-Asfar)?" He said: "I am greatly infatuated with women, and I fear that if I see the women of Banu al-Asfar I will not be able to restrain myself from them and I will be tempted." ﴿Surely into temptation they have already fallen﴾ by staying behind. It is also read as "saqata" (he has fallen). ﴿And indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾, with no escape for them from it.

ﷺ

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 50:

﴿If good befalls you﴾ such as victory and booty, ﴿it grieves them; and if a misfortune strikes you﴾ such as hardship, ﴿they say, "We had already taken our precaution"﴾ by exercising caution, when we stayed behind ﴿before﴾ this act of disobedience ﴿and they turn away, rejoicing﴾ at what has befallen you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 51:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Nothing will ever befall us except what Allah has decreed for us﴾, its striking us; ﴿He is our Protector﴾, our Helper and the One who manages our affairs.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 52:

﴿Say, "Do you await for us [anything] except one of the two best outcomes?"﴾ Here the one of the two taa's (tā’) is omitted from the original, i.e., "do you await" (tarabbaṣūna, تَرَبَّصُونَ) means tantaẓirūna an yaqaʿa, "you wait for it to befall" — ﴿for us, except one of the two best⁠﴾ (al-ḥusnayayn, الحُسْنَيَيْن), the dual of ḥusnā, the feminine of aḥsan (best): victory or martyrdom.

﴿And we await for you﴾ (natarabbaṣ, نَتَرَبَّص), i.e., nantaẓir, ﴿that God will afflict you with a punishment from Him﴾ — with a calamity from the sky — ﴿or by our hands﴾ — by His permitting us to fight you. ﴿So wait⁠﴾ for that, ﴿indeed we are with you waiting⁠﴾ for your outcome.
Say, "Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you" (i.e., what you spend), in obedience to Allah. The imperative here carries the sense of a report (khabar).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 54:

﴿And nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them﴾ (read with the taa' or the yaa', i.e. "tuqbala" or "yuqbala"), ﴿except that﴾ (here "illa" is the agent, the subject, and "an tuqbala" is the object) ﴿they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they do not come to the prayer except while they are lazy﴾ (mutathaqqilun, i.e. reluctant, sluggish), ﴿and they do not spend except while they are unwilling﴾ (to spend), because they regard it as a burden (maghram, a loss or penalty).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 55:

﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you.﴾ That is, do not regard Our favours upon them as admirable; rather, they are a gradual leading-on (istidraj). ﴿Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the life of this world﴾ That is, to punish them, ﴿thereby in the life of this world﴾ through the hardship they endure in gathering it and the calamities that come with it. ﴿And that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers﴾ That is, come out (tazhaq: takhruj), ﴿while they are disbelievers﴾, so that He punishes them in the Hereafter with the most severe punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 56:

﴿They swear by Allah that they are surely of you﴾, i.e., believers, ﴿but they are not of you; rather, they are a people who are fearful﴾, who fear that you will treat them as you treat the polytheists, so they swear falsely out of taqiyya (dissimulation).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 57:

﴿Had they found a refuge﴾ to resort to, ﴿or caves﴾ (sardab, underground chambers), ﴿or a place to enter﴾ a place to go into, ﴿they would turn to it, rushing headlong﴾ they would hasten in entering it and in fleeing from you, with a speed that nothing could check, like an unbridled horse (al-faras al-jamuh).
﴿And among them are those who find fault with you﴾ (yaʿību-ka, criticizes you) ﴿concerning﴾ the distribution (qasm)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 59:

﴿If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them﴾ of the spoils and the like, ﴿and had said: "Allah is sufficient for us; Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger"﴾ from another spoil, what suffices us, ﴿indeed, we turn to Allah in hope﴾ that He will make us rich. The answer to ﴿if only﴾ [law] is: ﴿it would have been better for them﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 60:

﴿Indeed, the charities﴾ — the zakat — are to be spent ﴿on the poor﴾, those who do not find what falls into a sufficient position for their needs, ﴿and the needy﴾, those who do not find what suffices them, ﴿and those employed to collect them﴾, i.e., the charities, such as the collector (jabi), the divider (qasim), the scribe (katib), and the gatherer (hashir), ﴿and those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾, so that they may embrace Islam, or so that their Islam may be firmly established, or so that their peers may embrace Islam, or so that they may defend the Muslims. These categories: the first and the last do not receive today, according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, because Islam has become strong; unlike the other two, who do receive, according to the more correct view. ﴿And for﴾ freeing ﴿captives﴾, i.e., those under a contract of manumission (mukatabin), ﴿and debtors﴾, people in debt if they borrowed for other than a sinful purpose, or if they repented and have no means of repayment, or for reconciling between people, even if they are wealthy. ﴿And in the way of Allah﴾, i.e., those engaged in jihad who have no regular stipend, even if they are wealthy. ﴿And the wayfarer﴾, the one cut off on his journey. ﴿An obligation﴾ — it is in the accusative, governed by its implied verb. ﴿From Allah. And Allah is Knowing﴾ of His creation ﴿Wise﴾ in His action. Therefore it is not permissible to spend it on anyone other than these, nor to withhold a category of them when it is present; the imam shall divide it among them equally, though he may give some individuals of a category preference over others. The lam (in "for the poor") indicates that it is obligatory to cover all its individuals, but it is not obligatory on the owner of the wealth if he divides it, due to hardship; rather, it suffices to give three from each category, and not fewer, as the plural form indicates. The Sunnah has clarified that a condition for the recipient is that he be Muslim and not from the Banu Hashim or the Banu al-Muttalib.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 61:

﴿And among them﴾, i.e., among the hypocrites, ﴿are those who abuse the Prophet﴾ by finding fault with him and by relaying his words, ﴿and say﴾ when they are forbidden from that, lest it reach him, ﴿"He is an ear"﴾, i.e., he listens to every saying and accepts it; so when we swear to him that we did not say it, he believes us. ﴿Say﴾: he is ﴿an ear﴾ that listens, ﴿good for you﴾, not an ear that listens to evil. ﴿He believes in God and believes﴾, i.e., gives credence to, ﴿the believers﴾ in what they tell him, not to others. The lām is extra, for the distinction between the belief of submission and other than it. ﴿And a mercy﴾, with the raising (rafʿ) as a conjunction upon "ear", and with the lowering (jarr) as a conjunction upon "good".

﴿They swear by Allah to you﴾, O believers, concerning what has reached you of their harm to the Messenger, that they did not do it, ﴿in order to please you. But Allah and His Messenger are more worthy that they should please Him﴾ with obedience. The pronoun is kept singular, as in ﴿يُرْضُوهُ﴾ (yurdhūhu, "they should please Him"), because the two acts of pleasing (the pleasing of Allah and of His Messenger) imply one another (tawḥīd al-ḍamīr, "the unification of the pronoun"). Or the predicate (khabar, the complement of the subject) of "Allah and His Messenger" is omitted (maḥdhūf, "elided"), so that the sense is that Allah and His Messenger are more worthy. ﴿If they are believers﴾ truly.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 9, verse 63:

﴿Did they not know﴾ that ﴿whoever opposes⁠ [yuhadid] Allah and His Messenger, then indeed for him is the fire of Hell﴾ as recompense. (Here "annahu" means that the matter is: "whoever opposes" is the subject of the clause.)

﴿The hypocrites fear﴾ means they are afraid (yakhāf), ﴿that a sūrah (chapter) be sent down against them﴾, i.e., against the believers (al-mu'minīn), ﴿informing them of what is in their hearts﴾ of hypocrisy (nifāq), ﴿and yet they mock﴾ (yastahzi'ūn) ﴿Say: "Mock, [then]"﴾, an imperative of threat (amr tahdīd), ﴿"Indeed Allah will bring forth"﴾, i.e., will manifest (muzhir), ﴿"what you fear"﴾, namely its bringing forth from your hypocrisy.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 9, verse 65:**

﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ *lam* of oath (*lam al-qasam*, the particle of swearing) ﴿سَأَلْتَهُمْ﴾ about their mockery of you and the Qur'an, while they were travelling with you to Tabuk." ﴿﴾ "لَيَقُولُنَّ" ﴿مُعْتَذِرِينَ﴾ "Indeed we were only engaging in idle talk and play" ﴿فِي الْحَدِيثِ لِنَقْطَعَ بِهِ الطَّرِيقَ وَلَمْ نَقْصِدْ ذَلِكَ﴾ "Say" ﴿لَهُمْ﴾

Do not make excuses; you have disbelieved after your belief. That is, your disbelief has become apparent after you had shown belief.

﴿If We pardon a group among you﴾ — read yu'fa with ya' and in the passive form, and nu'adhdhib with nun and in the active form — ﴿because of their sincerity and repentance, like Jahsh ibn Himyar﴾ — ﴿We will punish a group﴾ — read with ta' and nun — ﴿because they were criminals﴾, persisting in hypocrisy and mockery.

The Hypocrites, men and women, are of one another: that is, they are alike in disbelief, like parts of a single thing. ﴿They enjoin what is reprehensible﴾, meaning disbelief and sins, ﴿and forbid what is right﴾, meaning faith and obedience. ﴿And they withhold their hands﴾, meaning they refrain from spending in the cause of obedience. ﴿They have forgotten Allah﴾, meaning they abandoned His obedience; ﴿so He has forgotten them﴾, meaning He abandoned them, withdrawing His kindness from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 68:

﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding therein; it is sufficient for them﴾ as recompense and punishment. ﴿And Allah has cursed them﴾ He removed them far from His mercy. ﴿And for them is a lasting punishment﴾ ﴿enduring﴾.

You (hypocrites) are like those before you, who were stronger than you and had more wealth and children, and they enjoyed their share (of worldly pleasures) — they enjoyed their portion (bi-khalaqihim) of the world, ﴿so you have enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed theirs﴾ — you, O hypocrites, enjoyed your portion (bi-khalaqikum), ﴿as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you plunged﴾ into falsehood and slander against the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿as they plunged﴾, i.e., like their plunging.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 70:

﴿Has there not come to them the news﴾ the report of ﴿those before them: the people of Noah, and ʿAad﴾ the people of Hud, ﴿and Thamud﴾ the people of Salih, ﴿and the people of Abraham, and the companions of Madyan﴾ the people of Shuʿayb, ﴿and the overturned cities﴾ the towns of the people of Lot, meaning their inhabitants. ﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾ with the miracles. So they denied them, and they were destroyed. ﴿It was not Allah who would wrong them﴾ by punishing them without a sin, ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾ by committing sin.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 71:

﴿And the believing men and the believing women are allies of one another; they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, establish prayer, give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those — Allah will have mercy on them. Indeed, Allah is Mighty﴾, who cannot be prevented by anything from carrying out His promise and His threat, ﴿Wise﴾, who places nothing except in its proper place.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 72:

﴿Allah has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and pleasant dwellings in the gardens of Eden (perpetual residence)﴾ ﴿and approval from Allah is greater﴾, greater than all of that.

O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers (with the sword) and the hypocrites (with the tongue and argument), and be harsh with them (by rebuking and expressing disdain). Their abode is Hell, and wretched is the destination (the return), it is.

﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say [it]﴾, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿what they did not say﴾, meaning the abuse against them that reached you. ﴿And they did say the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam﴾, meaning they openly showed disbelief after openly showing Islam. ﴿﴾ "And they intended what they did not attain" ﴿from the assassination of the Prophet on the night of al-'Aqabah, when he was returning from Tabuk, and they were more than ten men. Ammar ibn Yasir struck the faces of the mounts when they surrounded him, and they were turned back﴾. "And they took offense" ﴿disapproved﴾ "only that Allah and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty" ﴿with the spoils after their great need. The meaning is that they gained nothing from him except this, and it is not something to resent﴾. "So if they repent" ﴿from hypocrisy and believe in you﴾ "it will be better for them. And if they turn away" ﴿from faith﴾ "Allah will punish them with a painful torment in this world" ﴿by killing﴾ "and in the Hereafter" ﴿by the Fire﴾. "And they will have no protector on earth" ﴿to guard them from Him﴾ "nor any helper" ﴿to prevent them﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 75:

﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity, and we will surely be among the righteous."﴾ In it there is idgham (assimilation) of the taa' (of the original form, i.e. the taa' of tatasaddaqa) into the saad. ﴿And we will surely be among the righteous.﴾ This refers to Tha'labah ibn Hatib, who asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to supplicate that Allah grant him wealth, and with it he would give every person with a right his due. So he (ﷺ) supplicated for him, and Allah expanded his provision. He then abandoned the Friday prayer and congregational prayer, and withheld the zakat.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 76:

﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and turned away﴾ from obedience to Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 77:

﴿So He caused them to follow up hypocrisy﴾, i.e., He made its outcome (ʿāqibah) ﴿hypocrisy﴾ firmly established ﴿in their hearts until the Day when they meet Him﴾, i.e., Allah, which is the Day of Resurrection. Then, after that, he came to the Prophet ﷺ with his zakat and said: "Indeed Allah has prevented me from accepting it from you." So he began throwing dust on his head. Then he went to Abu Bakr, and he did not accept it; then to ʿUmar, and he did not accept it; then to ʿUthman, and he did not accept it, and he died during his time.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 78:

﴿Did they not know﴾ that is, the hypocrites, ﴿that Allah knows their secret﴾ what they conceal within themselves, ﴿and their private consultation﴾ what they confer about among themselves, ﴿and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen﴾ what is hidden from observation. When the verse of charity was revealed, a man came and gave a great deal in charity, and the hypocrites said: "He is showing off." And another man came and gave a sa' (a measure of about three kilograms of dates), and they said: "Allah is free of need from this man's charity." So it was revealed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 79:

﴿Those who﴾ is the subject (mubtada'). ﴿Find fault with﴾ means they criticize ﴿those who volunteer﴾, i.e., those who give voluntary charity (al-mutanaffilin), ﴿among the believers in their charity, and those who find nothing but their effort﴾, meaning their capacity, so they bring it, ﴿and mock them﴾. The predicate (al-khabar) is ﴿Allah mocks them﴾, meaning He requites them for their mockery.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 80:

﴿Ask forgiveness for them, O Muhammad, or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾ — an option given to him regarding asking forgiveness and abandoning it. He ﷺ said: "I was given the choice and I chose asking forgiveness," meaning asking forgiveness. Narrated by al-Bukhari. ﴿If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾ — it has been said that what is meant by "seventy" is hyperbole regarding the abundance of seeking forgiveness. In al-Bukhari there is a hadith: "If I knew that if I added to the seventy it would be forgiven, I would add to them." It has also been said that what is meant is the specific number, based on his (ﷺ) hadith also: "I will add to the seventy." Thus He made clear to him the finality of forgiveness's denial through the verse ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 9, verse 81:

﴿Those who were left behind⁠﻿ rejoiced⁠﻿ in their sitting⁠﻿ [at home]⁠﻿ — i.e., their staying behind⁠﻿ — ﴾ [Tabuk] ﴿contrary to the Messenger of God⁠﻿⁠﻿﴾ — i.e., after him — ﴿and they disliked to strive with their wealth and their selves in the way of God⁠﻿⁠﻿﴾. And they said — i.e., some of them said to others — ﴿Do not go forth in the heat⁠﻿⁠﻿﴾ — i.e., do not go out to the jihad — ﴿Say: The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat⁠﻿⁠﻿﴾ than Tabuk, so it is more fitting that they guard themselves against it by abandoning their staying behind ﴿if only they understood⁠﻿⁠﻿﴾ — i.e., knew that — they would not have stayed behind.
﴿So let them laugh a little﴾ in this world, ﴿and let them weep much﴾ in the Hereafter. This is a report about their state, expressed in the form of a command.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 83:

﴿So if Allah returns you﴾ (i.e., brings you back) ﴿from Tabuk﴾ ﴿to a group of them﴾ (i.e., of those among the hypocrites who stayed behind in Medina) ﴿and they ask your permission to go out﴾ with you ﴿to another campaign﴾ ﴿then say﴾ to them: ﴿"You shall never go out with me, and you shall never fight an enemy with me. Indeed, you were content to sit idle the first time, so sit with those who stay behind."﴾ (al-Khalifun, i.e., those who stay behind from the campaign, among the women, the children and others).

When the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed over Ibn Ubayy, ﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, nor stand at his grave﴾ was revealed, for burial or for visiting. ﴿Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and died while they were defiant﴾, meaning disbelievers.

﴿Let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them with these in this world, and that their souls depart﴾ ﴿وتَزْهَق﴾ (tazhaq): "takhruj" (depart, come out), meaning their souls leave their bodies while they are disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 86:

﴿And when a surah is sent down﴾, i.e., a portion of the Qur'an, ﴿[saying]: "Believe in Allah and strive with His Messenger"﴾, i.e., [to the effect] that ("an" = "bi-an"), ﴿the men of wealth among them ask your permission﴾, [i.e.,] those possessed of wealth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 87:

﴿They were content to be with the women who remain behind﴾ the plural of khālifah (khawālif), i.e., the women who remained behind in the houses. ﴿And a seal was set upon their hearts, so they do not understand﴾ the good.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 88:

﴿But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their selves; and for them are the good things; and it is they who are the successful.﴾ (in) the worldly life and the Hereafter. ﴿And it is they who are the successful﴾, i.e., the winners.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 90:

﴿And those who made excuses among the Bedouins came [to the Prophet ﷺ]﴾, with the ta' (of the root) assimilated into the dal, originally al-mu'tadhirun (the ones making excuses), meaning al-ma'dhurun (those who have valid excuses). It was also read this way. ﴿among the Bedouins﴾ [came] to the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿so that they might be given leave﴾ to remain behind because of their excuse, so he gave them leave. ﴿And those who lied to Allah and His Messenger sat [at home]﴾, in claiming faith, from among the hypocritical Bedouins, refraining from coming to offer an excuse.

There is no blame on the weak (such as the elderly) ﴿nor on the sick (such as the blind and the lame)﴾, ﴿nor on those who find nothing to spend﴾ on the jihad, ﴿for them there is no sin (ḥaraj, "blame" or "sin") in staying behind from it, when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾ while they sit at home, by not spreading discouragement, not discouraging others, and by obedience. ﴿There is no way (sabīl, "path" or "means") against the good-doers﴾ in this matter, by way of blame. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾ toward them, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them in granting this leniency.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 9, verse 92:

﴿Nor [is there blame] upon those who came to you that you might provide them with mounts,﴾ [meaning] with you, to the raid (al-ghazw). They were seven men from the Ansar, and it was said they were the sons of Muqarrin. ﴿You said, "I cannot find anything to mount you on."﴾ The clause ﴿you said﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal). ﴿They turned back﴾ is the response (jawab) of ﴿idha﴾ (when), meaning they departed. ﴿While their eyes overflowed﴾ means flowed, ﴿with tears﴾ here the particle ﴿min﴾ is explanatory (lil-bayan), ﴿the tears, out of grief﴾ on account of ﴿their not finding what they could spend﴾ on the jihad.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 9, verse 93:

﴿The blame is only upon those who ask your permission while they are rich.﴾ [They ask permission] to stay behind (fi al-takhallufi). ﴿They are content to be with those who stay behind (al-khawalif), and Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.﴾ The like of it has preceded.

They will make excuses to you when you return to them (from the campaign). Say: "Do not make excuses; we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news," that is, He has told us of your circumstances. "And Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger; then you will be returned" by the resurrection "to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed," that is, Allah, "and He will inform you of what you used to do," meaning He will recompense you for it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 9, verse 95:

﴿They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them﴾ (i.e., come back to them) ﴿from Tabuk﴾ that they have excuse for staying behind. ﴿So that you may leave them alone﴾ by abandoning reproach. ﴿So leave them alone; indeed they are filth﴾ (qadhar, i.e., impure) because of the corruption of their inner selves.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 96:

﴿They swear to you that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ That is, with them; and your being pleased with them does not benefit when Allah is displeased.

The Bedouin Arabs are more intense in disbelief and hypocrisy (ash-shadd kufran wa nifaqan) than the people of the towns, because of their harshness, the coarseness of their natures, and their distance from hearing the Qur'an. "And more likely" (wa ajdar) means more fitting, "that" (an) means that, "they should not know the limits (hudud) of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger" (ma anzala Allah ʿala rasulihi), of the rulings and laws (ahkam wa shara'i'). "And Allah is All-Knowing" (ʿalim) of His creation, "All-Wise" (hakim) in His dealings with them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 98:

﴿And among the Bedouin is he who takes what he spends [in the way of Allah] as a loss (maghram)﴾, a penalty and a ruin, because he does not hope for its reward but spends it out of fear. They are the Banu Asad and Ghatafan. ﴿And he awaits for you the turns [of fortune] (al-dawa'ir)﴾, the turns of time, that they may turn against you, so that he may be rid [of you]. ﴿For them is a circle of evil (da'irat al-su')﴾, with a dammah or a fatha [on the first letter], meaning the torment and destruction revolve upon them, not upon you. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of the words of His servants, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of their deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 99:

﴿And among the Bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day﴾ like Juhayna and Muzayna (two tribes), ﴿and take what they spend in the way of God as means of nearness﴾ that brings them closer ﴿to God﴾, as a means to ﴿and prayers﴾, meaning supplications, ﴿of the Messenger﴾ for them. ﴿Indeed, it﴾, i.e. their expenditure, ﴿is a means of nearness﴾, pronounced with a ḍamma on the rāʾ (قُرْبَة, qurbah) and also with a sukūn (qurbah with the rāʾ unvowelled, read as قُرْبَة and قُرْبَة). ﴿For them﴾ with Him, ﴿God will admit them into His mercy﴾, meaning His Garden. ﴿Indeed God is Forgiving﴾ to those who obey Him, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 100:

﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants (muhajirun) and the Helpers (ansar)﴾ — they are those who witnessed Badr, or all of the Companions (sahaba) — ﴿and those who followed them﴾ until the Day of Resurrection ﴿in excellence﴾ in action ﴿Allah is well pleased with them﴾ through His obedience ﴿and they are well pleased with Him﴾ through His reward ﴿and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. And in one reading (qira'a) there is an addition of "min" (مِن), so that it reads ﴿من تحتها﴾ ("from beneath them").

And among those around you of the Bedouin (al-a'rab) are hypocrites (munafiqun), such as Aslam, Ashja' and Ghifar; and among the people of Medina too are hypocrites. They have persisted in hypocrisy (maradu 'ala al-nifaq): they insisted upon it and continued in it. "You do not know them" [meaning, you do not know them] by disgrace or by killing in this world, and by the punishment of the grave. "Then they will be returned" in the Hereafter "to a great punishment," which is the Fire.

(And) there are others (qawm ākharūn), a mubtada' (subject), who have acknowledged their sins (iʿtarafū bi-dhunūbihim), from staying behind (min al-takhallufi), a descriptive clause (naʿt), and the predicate (khabar) is: they mixed a righteous deed (khalaṭū ʿamalan ṣāliḥan), which was their striving (jihādahum) before that, or their acknowledgment of their sins, or other than that, with another, an evil deed (wa-ākhar sayyi'an), which was their staying behind. "It may be that Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah and a group who tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque when news reached them of what had been revealed about those who stayed behind, and they swore that none would release them except the Prophet (ﷺ). So he released them when it was revealed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 103:

﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them﴾ from their sins. So he took a third of their wealth and gave it in charity. ﴿And pray for them﴾, i.e., supplicate for them. ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, a mercy; and it was said, a tranquillity, through the acceptance of their repentance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 104:

﴿Did they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities?﴾ "Yaqbalu" (accepts), and the interrogative is for affirmation (taqrir), and its purpose is to stir them up to repentance and charity. ﴿And that Allah is the Accepter of repentance﴾ from His servants by accepting their repentance, ﴿the Merciful﴾ toward them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 105:

﴿Say﴾ to them, or to people: ﴿Work﴾ as you wish. ﴿Allah will see your work, and His Messenger, and the believers. And you will be returned﴾ through the Resurrection ﴿to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, i.e., Allah, ﴿and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, and He will recompense you for it.

And [there are] others [of those who stayed behind] who are deferred (murjawn), by hamz or without it, held back from repentance, awaiting the command of Allah concerning them, to do with them as He wills: ﴿either He will punish them﴾ by causing them to die without repentance, ﴿or He will turn to them in forgiveness﴾. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His dealings with them. They were the three who came after: Marrah ibn al-Rabi‘, Ka‘b ibn Malik, and Hilal ibn Umayyah, who stayed behind out of laziness and inclination to ease, not hypocrisy, and did not offer an excuse to the Prophet (ﷺ) as others did. So his matter was suspended for fifty nights, and the people shunned them, until their repentance was revealed afterward.

﴿And﴾ among them are ﴿those who took a mosque﴾, and they were twelve of the hypocrites, ﴿for harm﴾ by causing injury to the people of the Mosque of Quba, ﴿and disbelief﴾ because they built it on the order of Abu 'Amir al-Rahib, so that it would be a stronghold for him, where whoever came from his side would stop. He had gone to bring armies from Qayṣar (Caesar) to fight the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿And division among the believers﴾, who prayed at Quba, by having some of them pray in their mosque. ﴿And an ambush﴾, a lying in wait ﴿for him who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before﴾, that is, before its construction, and he is the aforementioned Abu 'Amir. ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but﴾ the ﴿good﴾ deed, which is kindness to the needy in rain and heat and the widening of the space for the Muslims, when they built it"﴾. ﴿And Allah bears witness that they are surely liars﴾ in that. They had asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to pray in it, so this was revealed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 108:

﴿Do not stand﴾ (i.e., do not pray) ﴿in it, ever.﴾ So he sent a group who demolished it and burned it, and they made its site a dunghill into which carrion was thrown. ﴿A mosque founded﴾ its foundations were laid ﴿upon piety from the first day﴾ it was established on the day you arrived in the abode of the Hijrah, and this is the Mosque of Quba, as is mentioned in al-Bukhari. ﴿Is more worthy﴾ than it ﴿that﴾ i.e., that ﴿you stand﴾ (i.e., pray) ﴿in it. In it are men﴾ they are the Ansar ﴿who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves.﴾ i.e., He rewards them for it. The ta' in the original (yatatahharu) is assimilated into the ta' (tatahharu becoming yatatahharu). Ibn Khuzaymah narrated in his Sahih, from Uwaymir ibn Sa'idah: "The Prophet (ﷺ) came to them at the Mosque of Quba and said: 'Indeed Allah, the Exalted, has praised you well concerning the purification in the matter of your mosque. What is this purification with which you purify yourselves?' They said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know of nothing except that we had neighbours among the Jews, and they used to wash their posteriors after defecation, so we washed as they washed.'" And in a hadith narrated by al-Bazzar: they said, "We follow the stones with water." He said, "That is it, so hold fast to it."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 109:

﴿Is one who founded his building upon taqwa (fear) of﴾ Allah ﴿and⁠﴾ hope for ﴿His pleasure﴾ from Him ﴿better, or one who founded his building upon the edge (shafa) of a crumbling (jurf) cliff﴾ — the rā' may be vowelled with a ḍammah or left sukūn — its side ﴿hanging (hār)﴾ overlooking collapse ﴿so that it collapsed with him﴾ — it fell together with its builder ﴿into the Fire of Hell﴾? ﴿It is better⁠﴾ — an excellent parable for building upon the opposite of taqwa, with regard to its outcome. The interrogative is for affirmation, meaning: the first is better, and it is the example of the Masjid of Quba', while the second is the example of the Masjid of Dirar.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 110:

﴿Their building which they built will not cease to be a source of doubt﴾ (shakkan, a doubt) ﴿in their hearts, unless their hearts are cut apart﴾ (tanfasil, separated) ﴿by their dying﴾. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His dealings with them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 111:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth﴾ by their expending them in His obedience, such as jihad, ﴿in exchange for their having Paradise. They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed﴾. This sentence is a resumptive explanation (jumlah isti'naf, a new sentence that explains) of the purchase. In another reading (qira'ah), the passive verb is put first, meaning: so some of them are killed and the rest fight. ﴿A promise binding upon Him﴾: both words (wa'dan and haqqan) are verbal nouns (masdar) in the accusative, governed by their omitted verb. ﴿In the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah?﴾ meaning: no one is more faithful to it than Him. ﴿So rejoice﴾: there is a shift (iltifat) here from the third person (ghaybah) to the second person. ﴿in your bargain which you have made. That is the great achievement﴾ meaning: that sale is the great success that attains the ultimate goal sought.

﴿Those who repent﴾ is in the nominative as an expression of praise, with an implied subject (*mubtada'*, the subject of a nominal sentence), [who repent] from polytheism (*shirk*) and hypocrisy. ﴿Those who worship﴾ are those who devote their worship sincerely to God. ﴿Those who praise﴾ are those who praise Him in every state. ﴿Those who wander﴾ are those who fast. ﴿Those who bow and prostrate﴾, i.e., those who pray. ﴿Those who enjoin the good and forbid the wrong, and who guard the limits of God﴾, that is, His rulings, by acting upon them. ﴿And give good news to the believers﴾ of Paradise.

Revealed concerning the Prophet's (ﷺ) seeking forgiveness for his paternal uncle Abu Talib, was also the seeking of forgiveness by some of the Companions for their two polytheist parents: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were of near kin﴾ (dhawi qurba, i.e., relatives) ﴿after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ (al-Nar), by dying upon disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 114:

﴿And the seeking of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾, by his saying: "I will ask forgiveness of my Lord for you", hoping that he would become Muslim. ﴿But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah﴾, by his dying in disbelief, ﴿he disassociated himself from him﴾ and abandoned seeking forgiveness for him. ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was ever many-sighing (awwah), [i.e.,] much in supplication and invocation﴾, ﴿forbearing﴾, patient over harm.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 115:

﴿And Allah would not misguide a people after He had guided them﴾ to Islam, ﴿until He makes clear to them what they should beware of﴾ of action, so that they do not beware of it and thus deserve to be misguided. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, and among them is who deserves misguidance and guidance.

Indeed, Allah—to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death. And you have, ﴿apart from Allah﴾, O people, ﴿no ally﴾ (i.e., other than Him) who would protect you from Him, ﴿nor any helper﴾ who would prevent you from His harm.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 117:

﴿Indeed, Allah turned in forgiveness⦗mercy⦘﴾ i.e., He continued His acceptance of repentance (tawbah) ﴿upon the Prophet, and the Emigrants (muhajirun) and the Helpers (ansar) who followed him in the hour of hardship (al-'usrah)﴾ i.e., its time, which was their condition during the expedition to Tabuk, when two men would share a single date, and ten men would take turns riding a single camel, and the heat intensified until they drank the contents of the stomach (al-farth)﴿, after the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved﴾ (read with ta' and ya', meaning "inclined") ﴿from following him toward staying behind, because of the severity they were in﴾ ﴿then He turned in forgiveness toward them﴾ by making them steadfast.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 118:

﴿And﴾ He turned [in mercy] ﴿to the three who were left behind﴾ from repentance toward them, as indicated by ﴿until, when the earth was closed in on them despite its vastness﴾, i.e., despite its spaciousness, its expanse, so that they found no place in which to be at ease, ﴿and their souls were closed in on them﴾, i.e., their hearts, from distress and loneliness at the delay of their repentance, so that no joy or comfort could contain them. ﴿And they became certain﴾, ﴿that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned [in mercy] to them﴾, i.e., granted them success in repenting.
O you who have believed, fear Allah by abandoning His disobedience, and be with the truthful (al-sadiqin) in faith and covenants, by adhering to truthfulness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 120:

﴿It was not fitting for the people of Madinah and for the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of God﴾ when he went out to fight, ﴿nor to prefer their own selves over his self﴾ by sparing themselves from what he himself accepted of hardships. This is a prohibition in the form of a statement. ﴿That﴾ i.e., the prohibition against remaining behind, ﴿because﴾ ﴿because of the fact that﴾ "they" ﴿will not be afflicted with thirst﴾ ﴿thirst﴾ "nor fatigue" ﴿weariness﴾ "nor hunger" ﴿hunger﴾ "in the way of God, nor do they tread any path" ﴿a verbal noun meaning treading﴾ "that enrages" ﴿angers﴾ "the disbelievers, nor do they gain anything from an enemy" ﴿by God﴾ "gain" ﴿killing, or taking captives, or plunder﴾ "except that a righteous deed is recorded for them because of it" ﴿so that they may be rewarded for it﴾ "Indeed God does not waste the reward of the good-doers" ﴿i.e., their reward; rather He will repay them﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 121:

﴿And they spend not⁠ ⁠﴾ therein ﴿any expenditure, small⁠ ⁠﴾ even a date, ﴿nor large,⁠ nor do they cross any valley⁠﴾ in the journey ﴿except that it is written for them⁠﴾ thereby a righteous deed ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do⁠﴾ i.e., their reward.

When they were rebuked for lagging behind, and the Prophet (ﷺ) sent out a detachment (sariyya), they all went out to fight, so there was revealed: ﴿It was not for the believers to go forth all together﴾ to the battle, ﴿So why did not a group from every division﴾ (firqa, a tribe) ﴿of them go forth, a party﴾ (ta'ifa, a group), while the rest remained behind ﴿that they might gain understanding in the religion﴾, i.e., those who remained behind, ﴿and warn their people when they return to them﴾ from the battle, by teaching them what they had learned of the rulings, ﴿that they may beware﴾ of the punishment of Allah by complying with His command and avoiding His prohibition. Ibn 'Abbas said: this [verse] is specific to the detachments (sara'ya), and the one before it [applies] to the prohibition of a single person lagging behind when the Prophet (ﷺ) goes out [to battle].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 123:

﴿O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers﴾, i.e., the nearest of them to the nearest. ﴿And let them find in you harshness﴾, i.e., severity; meaning, be harsh toward them. ﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous﴾ by way of aid and victory.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 124:

﴿And when a surah is sent down﴾ from the Qur'an, ﴿among them﴾, i.e., among the hypocrites, ﴿is one who says﴾ to his companions, mockingly, ﴿"Which of you has had its faith increased by this?"﴾ meaning, its affirmation. ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith﴾ due to their affirming it, ﴿and they rejoice﴾, i.e., they are glad at it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 9, verse 125:

﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ (i.e., weakness of belief) ﴿it has increased them in filth upon their filth﴾ (i.e., disbelief added to their disbelief), because of their disbelief in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 126:

﴿Do they not see﴾ with the ya' (i.e., the hypocrites), and with the ta' (addressing you, O believers), ﴿that they are tested﴾, that is, they are afflicted ﴿once or twice every year﴾ with drought and sickness. ﴿Yet they do not repent﴾ from their hypocrisy, ﴿nor do they take heed﴾, that is, they are not admonished.

And when a surah is revealed mentioning them [the hypocrites], and the Prophet ﷺ recites it, some of them glance at one another, [wanting to flee, saying:] "Does anyone see you?" [when you rise. If no one sees them, they leave; otherwise they stay.] Then they turn away [from faith, into their disbelief]. God has turned their hearts [away from guidance] because they are a people who do not understand [the truth, since they do not reflect upon it].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 128:

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, i.e., from among you: Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Grievous to him is your suffering﴾ — ʿanitum (ʿanat), i.e., your hardship (mashaqqatakum) and encountering what you dislike. ﴿Ardently desirous of you﴾ that you be guided. ﴿For the believers, full of kindness﴾ — shadid al-raḥma (intensely merciful). ﴿Merciful﴾ — he wishes good for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 9, verse 129:

﴿Then if they turn away﴾ from believing in you, ﴿say: "Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but He. In Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne"﴾ (al-Kursi, the Throne), ﴿the Mighty﴾. He singled it out for mention because it is the greatest of the created things. Al-Hakim narrated in al-Mustadrak from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "The last verse to be revealed was ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ up to the end of the surah."
